newsitem.title: CANADA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-TORONTO FANS SAY GILMOUR TRADE SAD, BUT NECESSARY.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-TORONTO FANS SAY GILMOUR TRADE SAD, BUT NECESSARY.

text.p: Toronto hockey fans had mixed emotions after the struggling Maple Leafs traded popular captain Doug Gilmour to the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday.

Fans said they were sad to see the 33-year-old Gilmour go in Tuesday's five-player deal, but added that the cellar-dwelling Leafs needed the young players acquired for Gilmour and defenceman Dave Ellett.
"The guy's a great player," said Mike Samek, an automotive parts salesman and lifetime Leafs fan. "He's a throwback to the old-time guys who played with heart."

A sentimental favourite with fans, Gilmour, who has 15 goals and 45 assists this season, was named captain of the Leafs on August 18, 1994, following a season in which he led long-suffering Toronto to within one win of the Stanley Cup Finals.
During his Toronto stay, he appeared on television commercials for milk painted as a cow and was kissed on national television by colourful Canadian hockey commentator Don Cherry.
The Kingston, Ontario native began his career in St Louis in 1983 before joining the Calgary Flames, who he helped lead to a Stanley Cup championship in 1989.
He was acquired by Toronto in January, 1992 in a 10-player trade with the Flames.

Tuesday's trade came at a low point for Toronto's National Hockey League franchise, which is mired in last place Central Division with a 36-22-4 record and tied for the league-worst in points (48) with Boston and San Jose.
Patrons at Wayne Gretzky's sports restaurant in downtown Toronto were upset that the Leafs did not get a better deal.
"They (the patrons) said it was a bad trade," said a bartender named Stephanie. "They said we could have gotten more for Gilmour."
The Leafs traded the two veterans for a trio of untested youngsters -- defenceman Jason Smith, 23, 22-year-old forward Steve Sullivan and minor league forward Alyn McCauley.
"Personally, I'll really miss these two veteran players," Toronto General Manager Cliff Fletcher said.
"They have great character and I'm sure the New Jersey Devils are excited about getting them and it will substantially help their chances of getting through that tough Eastern Conference."
But he said the Leafs were intent on adding young players in a bid to rebuild the ageing, floundering team.
